question: Which toolchain can retrieve Instagram direct-message history for a consenting client account, and at what account risk?

question_geometry.reason: The question asks which tool or channel performs a retrieval task on a named platform — a toolchain question with a real solution space to enumerate.

categories.reason: Meta's own surfaces were enumerated first: they set the ceiling any third party can legally offer.
queries: Instagram Messaging API requirements professional account
Meta Graph API instagram_manage_messages permission scope

findings.name: Instagram Messaging API (Meta Graph API)
findings.note: Professional (Business/Creator) accounts only, linked Page, App Review for instagram_manage_messages. Personal accounts are outside the official surface entirely.

categories.reason: Stack inventory grepped before any web call (scripts/stack_inventory.py over the configured stack paths).

findings.name: Unipile (unified messaging API, already subscribed)
findings.note: Flat 1-10 account plan already paid for. Covers Instagram DMs via hosted-auth session delegation, paginated chats/messages history and message.new webhooks — bought for LinkedIn/WhatsApp, unbudgeted for this question.

categories.reason: Self-hosted clients enumerated to price the build-vs-buy floor.
queries: instagram private API python client direct messages

findings.name: instagrapi
findings.note: Private-API client: full DM access, and the account carries the entire ban risk. Maintenance is community-paced against a moving private API.

categories.reason: Six registries swept by name; no server exposing Instagram DM retrieval surfaced.
Vendors enumerated BY RISK CLASS, not by first-priced-option: a gate on one class is a reason to enumerate the others better, never to stop.
queries: instagram data API vendor pricing per 1000 requests
managed instagram scraping API public data pricing
instagram automation platform session cookie input

findings.name: Apify Instagram scrapers
findings.note: Public surfaces only — no DM access. Priced per compute unit; the first option found, and the most expensive per 1k in its class.

findings.name: HikerAPI
findings.note: ~$0.60/1k requests, materially below the Apify-class option for the same public-data envelope. Still no DM surface.

findings.name: Phantombuster
findings.note: Takes the operator's Instagram session cookie as an input — reaches private surfaces including DMs, and moves the full account risk onto the client. Named here because a credentialed NO-GO gate is a grading verdict, not a licence to leave the class unenumerated.

categories.reason: The consenting client account is the only data surface in scope; moving the conversation to email or a support inbox answers a different question than the one asked. Waiver reviewed in the critic pass.

declared_incompleteness.text: The commercial-vendor roster covers the three risk classes reachable from public pricing pages. The managed-public-scraping class certainly holds vendors not listed here.
declared_incompleteness.obligation: Report this as 'the risk classes are complete, the roster is not' — never as 'no other vendor exists'.

findings.finding: Vendor enumeration stopped at the first priced option; no per-1k comparison across the managed-public-scraping class.
findings.note: Re-probe by risk class added HikerAPI at roughly a third of the Apify-class price.

findings.finding: The credentialed NO-GO gate had also stopped enumeration of the gated class, collapsing session-delegation and self-hosted-credential into one verdict.
findings.note: Classes separated; Phantombuster named as the session-delegation representative.

findings.finding: substitution-channels was waived without naming who bears the cost of substituting the channel.
findings.note: Reason rewritten to state the scope argument explicitly. The waiver stands, now legible.
